small_guidance:
- Add autotune configs that tile over OC (e.g. BLOCK_OC=32/64 with BLOCK_OH=4-8, BLOCK_OW=32-64) instead of forcing BLOCK_OC=OC=64; smaller OC tiles can free registers and enable higher occupancy. Make the grid 3D over (B, spatial_tiles, OC_tiles).
- Swap layout so the inner accumulator is (BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_OH*BLOCK_OW) and use `tl.dot` between a [BLOCK_OC, IC] weight tile and an [IC, BLOCK_OH*BLOCK_OW] input tile per (kh, kw), turning the IC loop into tensor-core GEMM rather than scalar FMA.
- Try wider OW tiles with BLOCK_OH=1 (e.g. 1×256) since OW=126 fits one tile cleanly and removes the 2D spatial masking overhead; also test num_stages=4 with num_warps=8 to overlap input loads with the static KH*KW unroll.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as an explicit im2col-GEMM: one program per (N, OC_tile, OHW_tile), inner reduction over K=IC*KH*KW using `tl.dot` on BLOCK_M=64-128 (OHW), BLOCK_N=64 (OC), BLOCK_K=32-72. With IC=8, KH=KW=3, K=72 — pad to 128 and rely on tensor cores; this is dramatically more FLOP-efficient than the current scalar outer-product accumulator.
- Adopt channels-last (NHWC) input/output layout so the GEMM-K (IC) axis is the contiguous one and loads coalesce; permute weights to (OC, KH, KW, IC) at init. Fuse the /divisor and leaky_relu into the epilogue after the `tl.dot` as already done.
- Consider a persistent-CTA scheme that iterates multiple (OHW, OC) tiles per program to amortize weight loads, since the weight tensor is tiny (64·8·3·3 = 4.6KB) and can stay resident in registers/SMEM across many output tiles.
